second_order: running and repairing a fake death joke
theme_note: The moderators and poster first present the fake death, then undo the presentation and offer a peace offering; what varies is making the joke, retracting its official-looking treatment, and trying to repair the upset.

second_order: arguing over what makes an acceptable April Fools joke
theme_note: Participants judge whether the death joke was funny or fit a positive Stargate sub and propose more obviously fictional alternatives; rejection, defense, explanation, and rewriting vary within the same argument over the joke boundary.

second_order: calling people together and pooling pixels
theme_note: These passages recruit people into a shared build and turn individual placements into calls for coordinates, backup, and pooled effort; they vary from opening proposals to answering calls while a small design is underway.

second_order: drafting and scaling down what to draw
theme_note: Members work on the drawing itself by drafting it, choosing secondary marks, sequencing animation, weighing scripts, and reducing the design to a maintainable chevron or point of origin; the techniques vary while the practice remains adjusting the image to what they can make.

second_order: looking for room and help around other groups
theme_note: Participants search for open coordinates and approach or enter neighboring groups for space, help, or another location; the passages vary between redirecting the build, asking permission, joining another group, and trying flags or taskbar space.

second_order: backing away and trying again after erasure
theme_note: People watch larger attempts get filled in or defended, abandon contested coordinates, and recount the defeats before trying elsewhere; what varies is whether the pressure comes from Green Lattice, EraseThePlace, changing locations, or too few people.

second_order: completing and caring for a very small Stargate
theme_note: The group reports the ministargate underway and completed, then gives concrete boundaries and neighbor-preserving instructions for keeping it safe and lively; work, completion, defense limits, animation, and low maintenance vary within caring for the tiny build.

second_order: celebrating and claiming something made it through r/place
theme_note: After placement ends, participants celebrate survival and claim a collective accomplishment; the earlier items specify the little Stargate, while the later title-only claim leaves what 'something' was unspecified.

second_order: waiting to see which successor canvas people use
theme_note: This single late passage makes joining a new canvas conditional on seeing where people actually go, rather than showing a move or new organizing.

second_order: telling another group to erase flags
theme_note: This contrary single-code theme preserves one participant's direct call for destructive action without merging it into the later neighbor-preserving work or treating the call as collective follow-through.
